title: Ordered Curvature spatially encodes stem cell fate via nuclear mechanotransduction
description: RNA-seq profiling of human fetal bone marrow stromal cells (fBMSCs) cultured on colloidal self-assembled pattern (cSAP) nanotopographic substrates with defined spatial curvature. Cells were seeded on three representative substrates (CC#1, CC#6, CC#16) and flat tissue culture polystyrene (TCP) controls under three culture regimes: (1) 7 days in growth medium (7d), (2) 7 days growth medium followed by 7 days growth medium (7a7L, 14-day time-matched non-induction control), and (3) 7 days growth medium followed by 7 days osteogenic induction medium (7a7A). Three biological replicates were collected per condition. This dataset was generated to investigate how nanoscale ordered curvature regulates transcriptomic programs associated with mechanotransduction, osteogenic commitment, and immunomodulatory fate decisions, and to distinguish nanotopography-driven priming effects from differentiation medium-induced responses.
